design:
**One renderer, Hub records only.** `_render_hub_agent_context` serves every run and both context routes. Whether an agent is known is `agent_row is not None`; synced session state is read only for quality gates, which have no Hub-native home yet.

**Facts supplied by the trigger.** Working directory, isolation and branch are passed in by `trigger_agent_directly`, which computed them for the process, so the text cannot disagree with where the run actually is. Outside a run (the routes) no workspace is described.

**Parts for Copilot.** Lines are tagged `stable`, `per_turn` or `tool_surface` as they are appended, because a Copilot agent receives the stable part once, in its custom agent file, and the rest with each prompt.

**Both directions of a grant.** Each grant is stated whether held or withheld, because the withheld case is the one that costs a turn.

**Exit condition in the context.** A turn with an open, phased document is told that ending without submitting it or calling `ask_user` is not a way to finish, because the instruction to use `ask_user` alone did not stop agents ending turns with questions in chat text.

lifecycle: Imported from openspec 2026-10-07; overhauled 2026-10-08 against the code at e25e059.
problem: An agent that is not told where it is, who its peers are, what it may call or what it may not do guesses, and its guesses are refused mid-turn, after the turn has already been spent.

requirements.rationale: A change to an agent, runner, charter, instructions or quality settings must reach the next run without any regeneration step. Its Codex part: not driven since 2026-08-29 (Codex plan cancelled).
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL render an agent's context from its current Hub records before every run and deliver it through the runner's mechanism: written to `<run workdir>/.agentweave/context/<agent>.md` and passed to the CLI for Claude and Codex, and for Copilot split into a stable part (written into the agent's Copilot custom agent) and per-turn and tool-surface parts sent with each prompt.

requirements.rationale: An agent cannot message a peer it was never told about. Archived agents are left out because sending to one is refused, and a lone agent gets no Team section because naming the absence invites it to wait for someone.
requirements.statement: The context SHALL name the project and, when the project has at least one other open agent, a Team section listing every open agent by name with its bound runner's CLI, its model and the names (never values) of its environment variables, marking the reading agent's own entry; identity and roster SHALL come from Hub records only, not from `agentweave.yml` or synced session state.

requirements.rationale: Stable guidance and per-turn facts change at different rates; an empty or placeholder section reads as a fact.
requirements.statement: The context SHALL be layered as: project profile and per-turn facts (workspace, specification, team, quality gates, capabilities), then project instructions, then the communication mode and tool surface, then the charter, and each section the Hub has nothing for (quality gates, instructions, team) SHALL be omitted rather than rendered empty or with invented defaults.

requirements.rationale: An agent the operator created and addressed is one the operator intends to act; a stand-down block once made every Hub-native agent ignore its instructions.
requirements.statement: `GET /agents/agent-context?agent=<name>` SHALL return the same rendered context with machine-readable fields (`agent`, `known`, `registered`, `charter_id`, `charter_name`, `missing`, `context`, `stable`, `per_turn`, `tool_surface`), where an agent is known exactly when the Hub has a record of it; an unknown agent SHALL get onboarding context telling it to ask the operator to register it, and a known agent SHALL never be told to withhold work, wait for assignment, or report to a principal or `agentweave.yml` declaration.

requirements.rationale: A direct charter lookup is kept for callers that know a charter but not an agent.
requirements.statement: `GET /agents/context?charter=<id>` SHALL return that project charter's content, preceded by the project instructions when there are any, with a hint to use the agent-context route for full context, and 404 for a charter of another project or none.

requirements.rationale: An agent uses the branch name to ask what it has already done; told the wrong branch it resolves its history wrongly, and an agent that guesses its directory is refused.
requirements.statement: For a run, the context SHALL state the absolute directory it executes in and whether that is an isolated checkout, naming the branch the process is actually on (the task's branch for a task checkout, the agent's own otherwise) and that peers work in checkouts it cannot see, or the shared project directory, saying so and claiming no isolation.

requirements.rationale: Left unsaid, an agent discovers the missing repository by running git and reads the failure as a broken machine.
requirements.statement: In a project whose directory is not a Git repository, the context SHALL say there is no isolated checkout or branch, that git should not be expected to work, and that any other agent works in the same directory where edits can overwrite each other.

requirements.rationale: Such a read is redundant at best and, outside the agent's permitted paths, is refused, turning delivered information into an apparent failure.
requirements.statement: The context SHALL NOT direct an agent to read a file whose contents it already carries, including the materialized context file itself.

requirements.rationale: Without the document path an agent guesses, fails, and falls back to a summary, which is how an implementation stops matching what was approved.
requirements.statement: When a turn is bound to a task that implements a specification document, the context SHALL name that document as what the work implements and say how to read it, SHALL NOT frame the turn as authoring a specification, and SHALL name it once when the operator is also viewing it.

requirements.rationale: A capability an agent does not know it holds is one it does not use; one it guesses at is a refusal in the middle of a spent turn.
requirements.statement: The context SHALL state each operator-conferred capability the agent holds: evidence decision (`can_accept_evidence`), reading peers' checkpoints (`can_read_checkpoints`) and recalling cited observations (`can_recall`), naming the tools that use it.

requirements.rationale: A reviewer once spent a whole turn before discovering it could not record its verdict, then wrote it into its isolated worktree where nobody reads it; a not-found is deliberately indistinguishable from absence, so the boundary must be stated up front.
requirements.statement: For each of those capabilities the agent does not hold, the context SHALL say so and what to do instead: that evidence decisions are the operator's and a verdict belongs in a message or on the task, that only its own checkpoints are listed, and that a not-found from `recall` on a cited id is this boundary rather than a missing record.

requirements.rationale: Recording the outcome after the fact is the fallback; telling the agent the exit condition up front is what makes asking through the tool the path of least resistance.
requirements.statement: When canonical context is assembled for a turn whose open specification document has a lifecycle phase, the context SHALL state that ending the turn without either submitting the document or calling `ask_user` is not a way to finish, and that questions written as reply text reach nobody.

requirements.rationale: Turn-start supply is a delivery guarantee; reads during a turn are allowed only where scoped to the agent's own work.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL place in each turn everything the agent needs to begin it - its queued inbound entries, the roster of its project's open agents, its charter and the project's instructions - so that no tool is needed to retrieve them, and no tool SHALL offer an agent another agent's queue, secrets, hidden operator state, or a way to alter its own configuration or scope.

requirements.rationale: An agent told a short name reached for the harness's own similarly named tool and reported the roster unreachable.
requirements.statement: The canonical context SHALL name the tools by the exact names the run's harness exposes where that naming is known (`mcp__agentweave__<tool>` for Claude, `agentweave-<tool>` for Copilot), say elsewhere that a harness may add a prefix, and, where the harness has similarly named tools of its own, say once that they are not AgentWeave's.

in_scope: The workspace, task specification, team and capability sections of the context.
The turn-start state the context carries: queued inbound entries, the roster, the charter and project instructions.
Naming the tools an agent may call by the names its harness exposes.
The exit condition stated for a turn on an open phased document.
non_goals: Each tool's description, parameters and accepted values, and the `aw-tool` notice: agent-tool-surface.
Review and firing briefings: agent-flows, agent-loops.
Which document the operator has open beside the conversation: spec-chat-session.
Recording a turn that ended with nothing written: turn-outcome-visibility.
Charter content itself (agent-charter) and project instructions (project-instructions).

summary: Before every run the Hub renders the model-facing context for an agent from its own records: the project, where the run executes, the task's specification, the team, quality gates, which capabilities the agent holds and which it does not, the project instructions, the tools it may call under the names its harness uses, and its charter. Everything a turn needs to begin is placed in it rather than fetched by a tool, and a turn on an open phased document is told what ending it requires. The same renderer answers `GET /agents/agent-context` outside any run, and an agent the Hub has no record of gets onboarding context instead.
title: Agent context onboarding
